pages.lesson:
LESSON: GUIDED WRITING: SENTENCES

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: ARABIC LANGUAGE
Strand: Writing 3.3 Guided Writing: Spelling (2 sessions) • Correct spelling of words • 
Topic 3.4: Guided Writing: Sentences

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Guided Writing: Sentences. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why is it good to write legibly?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. construct simple sentences using acquired vocabulary
2. appreciate writing for effective communication

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE LEARNING: GUIDED WRITING: SENTENCES
This lesson teaches Guided Writing: Sentences for Grade 6 ARABIC LANGUAGE.

STUDY STEPS
1. construct simple sentences using acquired vocabulary
   Practise this until you can do it without help.
2. appreciate writing for effective communication
   Practise this until you can do it without help.

HOW TO SHOW UNDERSTANDING
Explain the idea in your own words, give one Kenyan example, then complete the practice tasks.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Describe Guided Writing: Sentences using something at your school.

Example 2: Give a home/community example from your county.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Underline the key ideas about Guided Writing: Sentences above.
2. Explain Guided Writing: Sentences to a parent using one local example.
3. Write or draw three things that prove you understand Guided Writing: Sentences.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Guided Writing: Sentences with school or home examples.
2. Answer: Why is Guided Writing: Sentences important for a Grade 6 learner?
3. Prepare a one-minute oral presentation for a parent or teacher.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why is it good to write legibly?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. construct simple sentences using acquired vocabulary
2. appreciate writing for effective communication

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
